market_context: United States/general English; raw nuts compared per 100 g and 30 g/roughly 1-ounce serving
title: Cashews vs. almonds: nutrition differences

seo.title: Cashews vs. almonds: protein, fiber, fat, calories
seo.meta_description: Almonds provide more protein and nearly four times the fiber; cashews have slightly less fat and fewer calories but more carbohydrate and abundant copper.
seo.search_intent: Compare cashews and almonds for protein, fiber, carbohydrate, fat, calories and minerals using equal serving sizes.

excerpt: Cashews and almonds are close in calories but far apart in fiber and carbohydrate. Per 100 grams, almonds provide about 21 grams protein and 12.5 grams fiber; cashews provide about 18 grams protein and 3.3 grams fiber with substantially more starch.
content_html:
Cashews and almonds occupy the same snack category, but their nutrition profiles are not interchangeable. Almonds are higher in protein and dramatically higher in fiber; cashews contain somewhat less fat and considerably more carbohydrate.

Raw nuts per 100 g

NutrientCashewsAlmonds
Calories~553~579
Protein~18.2 g~21.2 g
Fat~43.9 g~49.9 g
Carbohydrate~30.2 g~21.6 g
Fiber~3.3 g~12.5 g
Magnesium~292 mg~270 mg

Almonds provide about 3 g more protein and 9.2 g more fiber per 100 g. Cashews contain about 6 g less fat and 26 fewer calories, but roughly 8.6 g more carbohydrate.

At a 30 g serving, calories are nearly a tie

Thirty grams of cashews is about 166 calories, 5.5 g protein, 13.2 g fat, 9.1 g carbohydrate, and 1.0 g fiber. The same weight of almonds is about 174 calories, 6.4 g protein, 15.0 g fat, 6.5 g carbohydrate, and 3.8 g fiber.

The calorie difference is only about 8 calories, while the fiber difference is close to 3 grams. That makes fiber a much more meaningful distinction than treating cashews as a low-calorie nut.

Why cashews are higher in carbohydrate

Cashews contain more starch than many other nuts. USDA’s legacy entry lists a substantial share of their roughly 30 g carbohydrate per 100 g as starch, which helps explain why a 30 g serving contains about 9 g carbohydrate versus about 6–7 g in almonds.

Both provide magnesium; cashews stand out for copper

Magnesium is similar: roughly 292 mg/100 g in cashews and 270 mg/100 g in almonds. At 30 g, that is about 88 versus 81 mg.

Cashews are particularly concentrated in copper at roughly 2.2 mg/100 g, so a 30 g portion supplies around 0.66 mg.

Almonds stand out for fiber and vitamin E

At 12.5 g fiber/100 g, almonds contain almost 3.8 times the fiber of cashews. They are also notably rich in alpha-tocopherol, the main form of vitamin E.

What about fat quality?

Unsaturated fats dominate in both nuts. Cashews contain roughly 43.9 g total fat and almonds 49.9 g per 100 g. Saturated fat is a minority of total fat in both, although the exact fatty-acid mix differs.

The useful takeaway

Almonds lead on protein, fiber, and vitamin E; cashews contain slightly less fat, more carbohydrate, and a great deal of copper. Their calorie difference is small—only about 8 calories in a 30 g serving—so choosing on nutrient profile makes more sense than choosing on calories alone.

faq.question: Which has more protein, cashews or almonds?
faq.answer: Almonds: about 21.2 g/100 g versus 18.2 g in cashews. At 30 g, that is roughly 6.4 versus 5.5 g.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Almonds by a large margin: around 12.5 g/100 g versus 3.3 g in cashews.

faq.question: Which has fewer calories?
faq.answer: Cashews by a small amount: about 553 versus 579 calories per 100 g; at a 30 g serving the difference is only about 8 calories.
